The retrieved evidence spans multiple points in 2024, with earlier sources now superseded by more recent data. As of mid-May 2024, only 658 tornadoes had been confirmed [d9], and preliminary reports through May 27 stood at 857 [d7]. By late October, the confirmed count had risen to 1,515 [d1]. According to NOAA's NCEI November 2024 report, the year-to-date U.S. preliminary tornado count through November reached 1,762, described as "among the highest tornado counts on record for the same January-November period" [d2]. The most complete picture comes from the final year-end assessment: 2024 ended as the second most active tornado year on record, with 1,880 preliminary reports and at least 1,759 confirmed tornadoes in the United States [d4]. Only 2004, with 1,817 confirmed tornadoes, had more [d4]. It is worth noting that final confirmed counts are typically slightly lower than preliminary counts, as some reports may reflect duplicate sightings of the same tornado [d2].
